messages:
Lina (Product): Uploaded a compact mock for the capacity card with inline min/max + a collapsed 'burst settings' micro-accordion. Fig link: https://figma.com/file/xyz789 — thoughts on copy and keyboard flow? :coffee: Marco (Design): Nice! I like the compactness. Two quick things: 1) the min/max stepper looks densely spaced on keyboard focus (outline overlaps adjacent text). 2) The pool selector uses a tiny chevron — maybe unclear that it's a menu. Sam (Eng): Re: focus outline — we can expand the hit target and shift the outline so it doesn't overlap. For the menu, we could add aria-haspopup and an explicit down-arrow icon that's larger. Also: when burst opens it currently shifts the whole card height causing page jump. Rhea (A11y): For keyboard users, collapsing/expanding must not steal focus unexpectedly. Pattern: keep toggle button in tab order, use aria-expanded and move focus to the first interactive item inside only if user activated with Enter/Space. Otherwise preserve focus. Also add an aria-live polite region for status updates like "Burst enabled" so screen reader users know state changes. Lina (Product): Good call on aria-live. Copy question: instead of 'Burst' label should we use 'Burst (short-term capacity)'? users confused what burst really means. Marco (Design): 'Burst' alone is terse; maybe 'Burst capacity' or 'Temporary burst'. We have very limited space on compact cards. Option: show 'Burst' with a hover tooltip that says 'temporary extra GPUs for peak load'. Sam (Eng): Tooltip is fine but tooltips are not accessible by keyboard by default. Use an info button with aria-describedby pointing to the tooltip text, or make tooltip reachable via focus. Rhea (A11y): Yes — implement tooltip as a focusable element with role="tooltip" and aria-hidden toggled. Example: `
Temporary extra GPUs for peak load; billed differently.
` Lina (Product): Another UX question: show pool price delta on hover or inline? Jonah wanted a '-30%' delta near pool name to surface cost. Thoughts? Marco (Design): Inline delta helps scanning but adds visual noise. Maybe show the delta as muted microcopy under pool name, with a color token for negative (green) to denote cheaper. Keep tooltip for details (preemptible behavior). Sam (Eng): technical note: we already compute price deltas server-side; just expose value. But watch localization (percent symbols and spacing). Also ensure we don't use color alone to communicate cheaper — need an icon or text to support color. Rhea (A11y): Absolutely — color alone fails WCAG for many. Add a down-arrow icon or explicit 'cheaper' text. Also ensure contrast of muted microcopy meets AA at small sizes; bump weight if needed. Lina (Product): Keyboard flow suggestion for compact card: Tab sequence = pool selector -> min stepper -> max stepper -> burst toggle -> (if expanded) burst slider -> confirm button. Escape collapses burst and returns to burst toggle. Is that feasible? Sam (Eng): Yes. We'll implement focus trap within the card when a modal is not used. For the inline accordion we'll ensure Escape triggers blur to the toggle. Avoid moving focus to document body. Marco (Design): Animations: don't animate height for the burst expand; animate opacity/transform on inner contents to avoid layout shift. Minimal motion also helps vestibular issues. Rhea (A11y): Good. Also ensure keyboard-visible focus styles are present for each control. Provide high-contrast focus ring option for users. Lina (Product): I'll update the figma and try the alternate label 'Burst capacity' with tooltip + small delta below pool name. Will add microcopy 'temporary, billed per-minute' to tooltip copy. DevOps Bot: note: rollout checklist — ensure new aria attributes don't regress our snapshot tests. I'll add an integration test to assert aria-expanded toggles and that burst panel has role=region. Sam (Eng): Perfect. I'll land a small PR toggling aria-hidden rather than full remount to keep slider state. Will also add keyboard interaction tests (Tab/Space/Escape). Lina (Product): thanks everyone — will post updated frames in ~2 hours. :sparkles:
